title: Tailscale infinitely loads on MacOS Sonoma
body:
### What is the issue?

Tailscale presents as "loading" after updating to Sonoma. Expected behavior: load, then connect.

### Steps to reproduce

Upgraded to MacOS Sonoma. Every few reboots tailscale will successfully connect, but quitting and reopening the service does not reproduce this. If it fails on startup, it will continuously fail.

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

Upgraded to MacOS Sonoma.

### OS

_No response_

### OS version

_No response_

### Tailscale version

_No response_

### Other software

N/A

### Bug report

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The template asks for a bug report because it allows us to find telemetry for the device. Since the app is able to run at least some times after a reboot, the bugreport menu item should work.

Is this the App Store, [Downloadable](https://<redacted-host>/stable/#macos), or CLI version of Tailscale?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Sorry about that, it appears it may have been a fluke, getting it to work. I haven't been able to reproduce that and gain access to the bugreport menu. This is on the App Store version, I've reinstalled it and attempted logging out/revoking the device from the admin console but that doesn't seem to be affecting it.

https://<redacted-host>/stable/#macos

Install the downloadable version of Tailscale, run it and then in the settings > Privacy & Security> Allow Tailscale to load

It will work after that

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Something about your machines are different than most the userbase (which statistically is fine). We need to figure out what that difference is so we can repro and investigate how to work around the issue.

Usually it's other networking software you forgot you installed or enabled or thought you disabled but it actually is still running/grubbing around in OS config.

Apple Private Relay? Other DNS tools? Other VPNs?

We want to help work around so please let us know everything that might've altered your machine in the past.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant4 Here's an exhaustive list of all the networking stuff I've had on my machine, in order:
- Private relay
- OpenVPN
- Tailscale
- Docker desktop
- Twingate (this is what has replaced tailscale, was not installed prior to this issue)

Here's the list of troubleshooting steps I've followed up to this point:
- Rebooted
- Uninstalled, reinstalled, and rebooted (this means clearing out all VPN configs, all hidden application files related to all VPN applications including tailscale, and actually uninstalling instead of just moving the app to the trash)
- Installed from package download instead of App Store

Tailscale isn't infinitely loading anymore, it's just not launching the login page so no VPN profile is ever installed. It's behaving as if it has no internet access, though I'm at a loss as to what would be preventing that. Once again, all the previous applications have been disabled and/or removed entirely for this testing. Private relay is disabled. Any additional troubleshooting advice is welcome.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> On reboot it will connect, but Chrome then fails DNS requests for most websites. Safari however works fine.

That could be https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/9468
Recent Chrome versions try much harder to use IPv6, and in some conditions keep trying even if IPv4 would work better.

An exit node with broken IPv6, and any confounding factor like a proxy, will likely break Chrome but leave Safari unaffected. Non-Linux exit nodes are especially likely to trigger this https://tailscale.com/kb/1177/kernel-vs-userspace-routers/

comments.body: @participant9 @participant5 adding this for posterity: your logs (`read tcp [::1]:51178->[::1]:10011: read: connection reset by peer`) indicate that the issue was caused by the macOS Content Filter blocking traffic meant for Tailscale servers. Switching to the Standalone variant should have fixed the issue. The content filter might have been enabled by your IT admin if you're using a work Mac.

comments.author: participant14
comments.body: We believe this has been fixed. If you're still encountering similar behavior, please create a new issue and include a [bug report](https://tailscale.com/kb/1227/bug-report/) after reproducing the behavior, and we can take another look.
